drift-pages

Monid's drift guard (deno task drift, design D28) checks pinned rates only where a vendor publishes machine-readable pricing, which today is Apify. This prototype reads the public HTML pricing pages of three connectors (Firecrawl, Exa, Apollo), has a model extract a strict rate table with a verbatim quote per row, and compares it to the usage.model pins from a real Monid compile. It raises an alarm and writes .output/drift-repin.json. It never edits a pin.

TypeScript / Deno 2DriftSuite drop-inalarm-only Source on GitHub · Walkthrough video · Eval

Left: deno task drift:pages --provider firecrawl against the real Firecrawl billing page (saved 2026-10-10). Right: same command after one planted edit, JSON format +4 to +5 credits / page. Model calls replay from recorded fixtures, so this is exactly what CI would print.

3. Eval: 20 saved pages

Base pages are the real public pages fetched on 2026-10-10. Price, unit and pricing-model changes are planted by hand, alongside no-change controls. A case passes only if the set of (check, docId) findings matches exactly. Click a row to see the planted edit, the extracted table and the findings.

no change: 6/6 · price change: 4/4 · unit change: 1/2 · regime change: 2/2 · new billable line: 1/2 · tier renamed, same price: 1/1 · table restructured to cards, same prices: 1/1 · page unreachable: 1/1 · promo banner: 1/1. 4. How it plugs into Monid

Copy scripts/drift/pages.ts and scripts/drift/pages/ into the repo and apply this 10-line patch (tested on monid-ai/monid@b3e7b0c: deno check passes and deno task drift --provider firecrawl runs). The weekly drift.yml job then covers these providers with no new workflow; it would need a free-tier model key as a repo secret.
